newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk leftist says main opposition backs censure.
newsitem.headline: Turk leftist says main opposition backs censure.

text.p: The leader of a Turkish leftist party said in remarks published on Saturday the main opposition Motherland Party (ANAP) had pledged its support for a censure motion against the Islamist-led government.
"We proposed a joint motion to ANAP. They said 'You prepare it and we will support it'," Republican People's Party (CHP) leader Deniz Baykal told the mass-circulation daily Milliyet in an interview.

The Democratic Left Party (DSP) has filed a similar censure motion against the government to "safeguard the secular system". The motions will be combined and debated by parliament in the last week of February.
The motion will effectively be a vote of confidence in the government alliance which has been strained by Islamist Welfare Party proposals during the Moslem holy month of Ramadan.
A reluctance by ANAP to commit itself on the censure vote has made the outcome uncertain. The leftist parties have a total 122 votes against the government's 279 in the 550-seat house.
ANAP has 128 deputies and the leftists say some dissident government MPs will support the motion, which needs an absolute majority of 276 to be carried.
The country's secular establishment has been unsettled by Welfare plans to lift a ban on women civil servants wearing Islamic headscarves and to construct mosques in secularist strongholds.
An anti-Israel rally in Ankara's Sincan district last week has also fuelled secularist anger and was followed by a parade of tanks in the Islamist-held area by the staunchly-secular army.
Turkey's first Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan formed a coalition with the conservative True Path Party (DYP) of Tansu Ciller last June.
Speaking at a dinner with Welfare MPs ahead of the Moslem Eid al-Fitr holiday, Deputy Prime Minster Ciller said the alliance would continue for the period of the coalition protocol.
The Eid al-Fitr holiday to celebrate the end of Ramadan will last from Sunday to Tuesday.
